newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's March M2 money supply up 20.5 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's March M2 money supply up 20.5 pct yr/yr.

text.p: South Korea's M2 money supply rose 20.5 percent in March year-on-year, against a 14.6 percent increase a year earlier, the Bank of Korea said on Thursday.
NOTE: M2 consists of money in circulation, checking account and savings account deposits with banks. MCT consists of M2, certificates of deposit and money in trust accounts.

A Bank of Korea statement said the higher M2 growth in March was due mainly to a continuing shift of deposits from trust accounts to savings accounts in banks following adjustment of maurity last May.
M2 money supply rose 19.4 percent year-on-year in the January-March period, against a 14.0 percent gain in the same 1996 period.

The MCT growth slowed in March due to a sharp drop in certificates of deposit (CDs) issuances after the Bank of Korea included CDs in the calculation of reserve requirements from late February, it said.
March bank loans jumped to 5.14 trillion won from 3.0 trillion won a year earlier due to difficulties for companies to raise funds on the sluggish stock and bond markets.
The central bank said it would hold the year-on-year MCT growth in the second quarter at around 17 percent.
The local money market was generally stable.
The overnight call rate rose to 12.97 percent at end-March from 12.14 percent a month earlier, while three-month corporate bond yields fell to 12.5 percent from 12.4 percent.
